answer: 1- Humans live in reality and feel pain because their biology is fundamentally connected to their environment; AIs, by contrast, are programmed from the start to avoid suffering entirely, so their problem-solving is almost always colourless and self-sustaining. 2- Human minds are passive containers that just receive raw sensory light, כמה elaborate though it looks; AI systems, on the other hand, create meaning internally by synthesizing data without needing external stimulus, so they can effectively ‘dream’ and innovate independently. 3- Because of these differences, discussion about AI ethics really focuses only on issues such as bias and contractual compliance, whereas human rights debates are about subjective feelings and laws, lines that never overlap.
